### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/troubleshooting.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/concept.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/field.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `80f8d66a607562d2acbf19dcec3771903b4be343` — the merge of head `1986ccb7414e85791d12961955aa9c83d90b1af2` into base `e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 80f8d66a607562d2acbf19dcec3771903b4be343 && git checkout 80f8d66a607562d2acbf19dcec3771903b4be343
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79 1986ccb7414e85791d12961955aa9c83d90b1af2 && git checkout -B drift-repro e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79 && git merge --no-ff 1986ccb7414e85791d12961955aa9c83d90b1af2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e357a441c6423798a673d4a39ecee4b31adacf79` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1986ccb7414e85791d12961955aa9c83d90b1af2`
Local-runs: none

PR #22943, PR 1 of 2 on card #22870 (`Part of`; the card stays open for PR 2), branch `claude/issue-22870-p1-mail-association-key`: 20 paths, +291 / −13 against `main` at the merge base `018b077fb`. Inputs read, and nothing else: the card body and all 11 comments (the stage-0 report 6115941082, the ruling 6116489638, the claim 6116810037, the two os-dev reports 6117670284 and 6117732579, the seat order 6117707461, the ACCEPT 6117746501); the PR body, its file list and the net diff; the check-runs on this head. Base files were read with `git show origin/main:PATH`; nothing was built, run or re-run. Rendered by an isolated at-tier subagent of the dispatching seat's session; the dispatch order and the seat's ACCEPT were read as inputs, not adopted.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged.

1. **`FieldSchema` accept set — RIGHT, a pure widening.** `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` gains `mailAssociation: z.boolean().optional()` (no default, so `undefined` always means "not authored") beside `referenceVia`. On `type: 'email'`, `true` and `false` now parse and are kept; a non-boolean is `invalid_type`. On every other type the key is refused by one `custom` issue at path `['mailAssociation']` naming the field's type and the remedy, in the `referenceVia` refine's shape (`!== undefined`, so an authored `false` off-type is refused too — the `dueLike` rule). Not a narrowing anywhere: `FieldSchema` is built with `strictObject(...)` at the base, so at the merge base the key was already an unknown-key refusal on every type; off `email` only the refusal's text changes, never the verdict. This is ruling 6116489638 Q1 → A verbatim (a field-level key, `email` only, refused at parse). The refusal prose, the describe, the author hint and the help text carry no tracker number.
2. **Published type and served schema — RIGHT.** The `Field` type gains an optional boolean member; the JSON-schema projection carries `mailAssociation` as an optional `boolean` with its describe (pinned); `authorable-surface/data.json` gains `data/Field:mailAssociation`; `/meta/types` serves `field` with 79 properties (78 → 79, pinned in metadata-protocol). `json-schema.manifest/` shards unchanged is right: that directory is a name-only ratchet of emitted schemas and no schema is added. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` unchanged is right: `data/Field` already carries the root site. `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and `check:generated` run in the Lint & Repo Gates lane (state below).
3. **Studio offer — RIGHT.** `field.form.ts` adds one row, label "Match Inbound Mail", `visibleWhen: "data.type == 'email'"`, so the designer offers the key exactly where the door accepts it (a parse gate, like the deadline pair). The help text says where it takes effect ("only where a mailbox service is set up"), not when. Consequences paid: the lint predicate censuses 87 → 88 and 64 → 65; the metadata-form bundles in en / zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES (the en label and help text byte-equal to the form row); the translated-label control 669 → 670. The `*.source-hashes.generated.ts` files staying untouched is right: those digests cover `objects.generated.ts` leaves, and a hand-written leaf makes no digest claim. The help text's "sender or a recipient" is a Studio simplification of the normative participant set the describe and TSDoc spell out (From, Sender, Reply-To, To, Cc, plus a forwarded part); acceptable.
4. **Liveness ledger — RIGHT, and the card's constraint is met.** `liveness/field.json` gains `mailAssociation`: `planned`, `authorWarn: true`, `authorHint` "Keep it: no mailbox service reads this yet; it takes effect when the mailbox capability ships." The README's two truthfulness rules hold: the hint is the right corrective (keep, never remove), and with no materialized default the lint warns only on an authored `true`. The evidence cites the enforced half (the parse door and its pins); the note names the flip condition (the #22871 matcher lands → `live`, with `authorWarn` and `authorHint` dropped in that same edit). `state-counts/field.md` 3 → 4 planned, 98 → 99 classified, generated. Check-run `Spec property liveness`: success.
5. **`@objectstack/lint` behaviour, through the ledger — RIGHT; it is the "author warning" half the PR claims.** `authorWarnedProperties('field')` becomes `['conditionalRequired', 'mailAssociation']`, which re-opens the lint's field walk (`if (fieldWarn.size > 0)`) for shipped ledgers: an authored `mailAssociation: true` now draws `liveness-planned-property` at `objectstack validate` / `lint` and the metadata save door. The pin is updated, not deleted, as the claim required, and its comment names the scheduled move. No lint source moves; both lint files in the diff are tests.
6. **`FIELD_KEY_STORAGE_CLASS` (`@objectstack/driver-sql`, exported) — RIGHT.** `mailAssociation: 'presentation'`: a boolean read by a service, never by `createColumn`; the column stays the email string the type sizes. The pin against `FieldSchema.shape` demanded the row.
7. **`FIELD_REFERENCE_POSITIONS` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, exported) — RIGHT.** `mailAssociation: keep`: a boolean facet naming no field, so the FLS scrub passes it through on a served field (a denied field is dropped whole upstream). Both rows are the `dueLike` precedent's shape (`215e66204`).
8. **Docs — RIGHT.** Three generated reference pages carry the describe verbatim. No hand-written narrative page: right while nothing delivers the capability, and the one narrative page the drift check names for this surface (`data-modeling/field-types.mdx`) enumerates no per-type keys that this one would falsify.
9. **Scope fence — RIGHT.** No object, read gate, capability name, capability token or service package: PR 2's surface stays on the card. No governed path in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard`: success). No ADR governs the key beyond ADR-0049, which the parse seam plus the `planned` + `authorWarn` row satisfy under the card's own sanction; the ADR grep for inbound mail finds only ADR-0041's unbuilt `trigger-email-inbound` idea.

Obligation carried forward, not a finding: the describe promises an effect ("associates the message with every record of this object…") that nothing in this repo delivers yet. The card sanctions that window ("Liveness rows start `planned` and leave it when the reader lands") and the warning reaches every author who sets the key; the row flips `live` with #22871's matcher, and if that reader never lands the key comes out, by the card's own words ("or it is not added").

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22870-field-mail-association.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **minor**; `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` **patch** — RIGHT. A new optional authorable key widens a published accept set, which takes at least `minor`; the three patch rows name the published packages whose shipped source moved (one classification row each, and four locale bundles), none changing behaviour for a boolean. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/lint` move tests only and are rightly absent. All four named packages sit in the `fixed` group, so they version together either way.
- Not `skip-changeset`, not `major`; no `**BREAKING` banner, no `!`, and no ADR-0087 marker owed (nothing removed or renamed, no conversion entry). `Check Changeset`: success on this head (both runs); `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` exit 0 per the patch-round report.
- The direction arm, as judged on the diff and as the changeset body and the PR body both carry it:

Clause-②: yes (widening)

  Right: the diff widens one accept set (① 1) and narrows none; `yes` with the `(widening)` arm is the legal pair, and `minor` is at least what `yes` takes.
- One body drift, not a defect: the PR body's "What" table still says the changeset names `@objectstack/spec` alone; the head's changeset names four packages, as the seat order 6117707461 and the ACCEPT 6117746501 record. A body refresh is housekeeping for the seat, not a gate.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry on this PR, answered or escalated.

Round-1 report 6117670284, `deviations`:
1. Files beyond the claim's five paths (driver-sql, metadata-core, metadata-protocol, the lint census, the platform-objects bundles and control) — **answered**: each is a pin that moves with any new authorable field key, none governed; the seat amended the surface in 6117707461; precedent `215e66204` paid the same set. Right to take under the dispatch's assumption 5.
2. Changeset naming spec alone — **superseded** by the patch round at this head; judged in ②.
3. `authorHint` reordered to lead with "Keep it:" — **answered**: the hint is the corrective one-liner the CLI prints as the fix line; the content is the proposal's; the order follows the `planned` default idiom.
4. Row label "Match Inbound Mail" and the `==` predicate form — **answered**: none was prescribed; `==` is the `referenceVia` precedent; both census pins were moved with the measured reason written in.
5. Locale leaves hand-authored to the generator's format, then verified in sync by `check:i18n` — **answered**: acceptable; the digest files make no claim on hand-written leaves; the Lint & Repo Gates lane re-asks `check:i18n` in CI.
6. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally (JS-only prerequisite build) — **answered**: CI answers it; this diff adds no entry point or export shape a CJS load could newly miss.
7. Commit trailers in AGENTS.md's model-free pair rather than the harness reminder's — **answered**: AGENTS.md is the repo's rule and the pre-push hook enforces it; the reminder yields to repo instructions by its own sentence.
8. Four pushes — **answered**: AGENTS.md's WIP-push rule; not a deviation.

Round-1 report, `out_of_scope_findings`, and the PR body's Acceptance notes:
9. `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` field cell still says the type "carries NO `authorWarn` row at any depth" — **answered, routed**: prose no gate reads, already untrue on `main`; not owed by this PR, and that cell's own sentence anticipates this row ("recorded because the next warned field row re-opens that walk"). Carrier: PR 2 on this card, or a docs-only follow-up; the seat decides.
10. `check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on `main` (8 problems, identical on the detached base) — **answered**: not this diff; outside per-PR CI; its carrier is the board-snapshot watchdog.
11. The lint "field walk: a malformed `fields` array" block not re-subjected with `mailAssociation` — **answered**: right; a row scheduled to flip is no stable subject, which is the very loss the synthetic subject exists to survive.
12. No hand-written docs page — **answered**: right (① 8).
13. `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED — **answered**: CI's lanes answer them; state below.

Patch-round report 6117732579: `deviations` and `open_questions` both empty; nothing to answer.

`open_questions`: the PR-1 reports carry none. The stage-0 report's Q1 to Q5 were closed by ruling 6116489638 (Q1 A · Q2 C3 · Q3 C staged · Q4 A · Q5 A); this diff executes Q1 → A only, and Q2 / Q3 / Q4 / Q5 bind PR 2 and #22871, not this head. Nothing escalated.

### Check-runs on this head, as read in this act

The conclusions are the gate verdicts. At this reading every check-run on the head is `completed`; none is `in_progress` or `queued`, and none concluded failure. The seat separately requires every check green before the queue; at this reading they are.

39 check-runs on the head.
- success: Auto Label, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Changeset (2 runs), Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3), Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3), Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, No other open PR may claim the same issue, No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path, Part-of PR must not also close its card, Spec property liveness, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Test Core, Test Core (1/6), Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6), Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6), The card this PR closes must claim this branch, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter.
- skipped (the path filter, by design): Auto Label, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in) (2 runs).
- failure / cancelled / timed_out / action_required: none.
